question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,1,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-2x+4y+4z=18.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+4y+4z & =18 \\ -2(-1)+4(2)+4z & =18 \\ 4z & =8 \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,2,2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,2,2⟩-⟨-2,1,5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-2,4,4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 4+(-3)\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-2+4-12|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-10|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{10}{6} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
